title: fix(plugin-security): the shipped sets stop copying the identity objects' declared row scopes
body:
Fixes #24484
Clause-②: no

The follow-up that ruling E′ item 3 (comment 6250748677 on #24164) names, as #24340's body records it. `organization_admin` (and so the derived `organization_admin_no_bypass`), `member_default` and `viewer_readonly` no longer carry copies of the row scope that thirteen identity objects now declare as their own `defaultRowScope` (declared by #24341). The thirteen are the seven SCIM projection tables, `sys_verification` and `sys_jwks`, and the `select` self scope of `sys_account`, `sys_team_member`, `sys_oauth_access_token` and `sys_oauth_refresh_token`. The security plugin's collection applies an object's default wherever the caller's held sets carry no policy for that object and operation, so rows do not move. Explain now names the object's default (`via: 'object_default'`) where it named a set's copy, as triage (6261582931) recorded the ruling accepts. No schema, `via` value, object declaration, `core` code or `packages/spec` file changes. It runs after #24136 (landed as b27f8ded5c), which edited the same file; this branch starts on the tree that holds it.

## Per-copy byte-identity readings (taken on `origin/main` 4a2ca57e74)

Each shipped set's policy for each candidate object, compared field by field (`name`, `object`, `operation`, `using`, `check`, `positions`, `enabled`) with the object's declared `defaultRowScope` plus `object`. Sets read: `organization_admin`, `organization_admin_no_bypass`, `member_default`, `viewer_readonly`.

| Family | Objects | Copies read | Identical | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SCIM | `sys_scim_user`, `sys_scim_subject`, `sys_scim_projection_grant`, `sys_scim_identity_tombstone`, `sys_scim_group`, `sys_scim_group_member`, `sys_scim_connection_binding` | 28 | 28 | dropped |
| credential | `sys_verification`, `sys_jwks` | 8 | 8 | dropped |
| `_self`, `select` | `sys_account`, `sys_team_member`, `sys_oauth_access_token`, `sys_oauth_refresh_token` | 16 | 16 | dropped |
| ledger | `sys_audit_log` (`sys_audit_log_org`) | 4 | 4 | **kept**, measured (below) |

56 of 56 copies were byte-identical. The only `'*'` policies in any shipped set are `member_default`'s `owner_only_writes` (`update`) and `owner_only_deletes` (`delete`), so after the drop each holder's `select` collection on the thirteen objects is empty and collects the default. On the head, the same reading finds only the four ledger copies left among the candidates, and the must-keep rows unchanged.

## What stays, and why

- **Pointer 6280763190's must-keep list**, untouched: `sys_user_self` (`all`) in `member_default`, and every `all` self scope (`sys_session`, `sys_two_factor`, `sys_user_preference`, `sys_api_key`, `sys_device_code`, `sys_oauth_consent`, `sys_oauth_application`, `sys_organization`). A member's `update` and `delete` collections hold the `'*'` ownership floor, so the default is never collected there. Also kept, outside the pointer's may-drop list: `sys_user`'s two `select` policies in `organization_admin` and `viewer_readonly` (they differ from the merged `sys_user` declaration), and `viewer_readonly`'s `select` spellings of objects whose default is `all` (they differ by operation).
- **`sys_audit_log_org`: kept, although it is byte-identical and on the pointer's may-drop list.** I measured it before dropping it. When no organization wall is enforced, `collectRLSPolicies` strips the platform's own tenant policies by provenance (`isPlatformTenantPolicy`). `platform-tenant-policies.ts` builds those provenance keys from the shipped sets' policies. With no set carrying the copy, the ledger's identical default is no longer recognised as the platform's. It survives the `single` strip as an authored tenant policy and narrows the ledger read. Ablation A3 below measures it under `single`: the viewer, both organization-admin variants and their agents went from all three ledger rows to one. `sys-audit-log-row-scope.test.ts` already pins the provenance half (the shipped copies are non-empty and each is a platform tenant policy). The helper's comment now says why the copy stays.

## Rows: the before/after served-ids run

New pin: `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/shipped-sets-identity-default-row-scope.test.ts`, modelled on `default-row-scope-declarations.test.ts`. It runs on the real `SecurityPlugin` + `ObjectQL` + `SqlDriver`, with the real declarations and a security catalog of the shipped sets. It covers three deployment shapes: walled with the platform baseline, walled with **no** platform baseline (`fallbackPermissionSet: null`, each principal resolves only the set it names), and `single`. The personas are a `member_default` holder, a `viewer_readonly` holder, both organization-admin variants, a user in no organization, delegated MCP agents for the member, the viewer and the organization admin (ruling B, 6278784335), and the platform administrator as a control. Each persona's served ids are asserted against the ids written out per family, on all 14 touched objects. They are also asserted equal to what the same deployment serves with the dropped copies spread back into the sets, on those objects plus `sys_user` and the eight `all` objects.

| Tree | Served-ids block (9 tests: 3 shapes x listed ids, copies restored, control) | After-state pins (explain, census, authored policy, no copy in any set) |
|---|---|---|
| `origin/main` 4a2ca57e74, sets unchanged | **9/9 pass** (plus the two keep pins and the private-object control) | 20 red, by design: the copies are still there |
| head e12d958692 | **9/9 pass** | all pass: 32/32 in the file |

## Explain moves, as ruled

Pinned per family against the copies-restored tree:

- SCIM: a member's record-grained explain of its own `sys_scim_user` row gives the rule `sys_scim_user_self` with `via: 'object_default'`. The tree with the copy gives `business_rls` and no `via`. The object-level read of `sys_scim_group` names `object default row scope 'sys_scim_group_none'` as its source, for all four set holders.
- `_self`: the same for `sys_account` / `sys_account_self`.
- credential: the object-level reads of `sys_verification` and `sys_jwks` name `sys_verification_none` / `sys_jwks_none`. The verdict is unchanged.
- `sys_audit_log_org`: **not moved**, because the copy is kept (above).
- Census: every human persona collects the object default on exactly the thirteen dropped objects' `select`, and on no other object or operation. With the copies restored, none. A delegated agent's own leg collects none (ruling B, whole).

## An authored policy still wins

A member who also holds an application set authoring `sys_account` `id == null` reads no `sys_account` row, and its collection is exactly that policy. The control is the same member without the set, who reads its own row under the default. Measured change: on 4a2ca57e74 this holder read its own row, because `member_default`'s copy was OR-ed in. An authored scope that left out the holder's own rows was widened back to them. Now the authored policy alone decides on that object and operation. This only ever narrows. No package or example in this tree authors a set policy on any of the thirteen objects (`git grep` over `packages`, `examples` and `apps`, tests excluded: 0 hits).

## Ablations (each pin red under the forbidden change, then restored)

Mutations went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, which checks the anchor count, the replacement count and the blob change on disk. Restores used `git checkout HEAD -- PATH` and were proven by the blob hash equalling HEAD's and by an empty `git diff HEAD`. No build was involved: the pin imports the sets from source. All four ran on 48e8f6dae5.

| Leg | Forbidden change | Red | Green, as expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1b | drop `member_default`'s `sys_oauth_application_self` (`all`) | keep pin (member write collection), census | served ids |
| A2 | drop `member_default`'s `sys_user_self` (`all`) | keep pin (write collection), `sys_user_self` stays `all` | served ids |
| A3 | drop `sys_audit_log_org` from all three sets | served ids under `single` (viewer, org admins and their agents: 3 ledger rows to 1), census, ledger-copy pin | served ids walled, both shapes |
| A4b | re-add `sys_account_self` (`select`) to `member_default` | no-copy pin, `_self` explain pin, census, authored-policy pin | served ids |

The first A1 and A4 attempts never ran. The tool refused both before any test, because their replacement overlapped their anchor. They were re-anchored as A1b and A4b.

## Also in this diff

- **Existing pins restated** where they asserted the copies stay: `default-row-scope-declarations.test.ts` (the thirteen declare the literal written out and no set carries it; the behaviour-neutrality comparison covers the ten declarers the sets still carry; the census expects the thirteen `select` defaults), `object-default-row-scope.test.ts` (`sys_scim_user` moves out of its byte-for-byte block into a block showing the declaration is the scope), and `rbac-objects.test.ts` (the `member_default` roster).
- **`private-credential-row-scope.test.ts`**: the header says where the scope now lives, and the `agent_x` persona (pointer 6280763190, last bullet) now has the shape its one producer emits: `userId` is the delegating member, `onBehalfOf.principalKind: 'human'`. `scim-projection-row-scope.test.ts` gets the same header correction, and its agent comment now states ruling B.
- **Outside the claim's declared file surface, comment-only, declared here:** the 13 `packages/platform-objects/src/identity/*.object.ts` comments above each `defaultRowScope` said "the shipped sets still carry it". That is false after this change. Only `//` lines changed; no declaration byte moved, and the declaration pin reads each value.
- **Deliberate correction of a pending release note:** `.changeset/24341-identity-objects-default-row-scope.md`. Three sentences stated that the shipped sets carry each policy, which this change makes false before that note ships. They now say each object's policy is either still carried or collected as the identical default. `check-empty-changeset` is red on purpose: its own text says a deliberate correction is confirmed on the PR, not routed around. **Please confirm this correction.** The other #24341 note sentences are about that change's own effect and stay true.
- New changeset: `.changeset/24484-sets-stop-copying-identity-defaults.md`, `@objectstack/plugin-security` `patch`.

## Tests and gates (head e12d958692)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security test`: 191 files, 3926 passed, 45 skipped, exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security typecheck` (tsc, scripts, test layer): exit 0. File-scoped `eslint --no-inline-config` on the seven touched plugin-security files: exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/platform-objects test`: 1195 passed. `typecheck`: exit 0.
- Closure build `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/plugin-security^...' build`: exit 0, run on the merged tree.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 67 families. Each was run locally with its exit captured before any pipe. 64 exited 0. `check-empty-changeset --base origin/main` exited 1: the deliberate correction above. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n` exited 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET (they need a whole-repo build), so they are NOT MEASURED here and CI's `Lint & Repo Gates` measures them. `--ran` reconciliation: 67 accounted for, 65 run, 2 NOT MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.
- `test:repo` was not run locally; CI's `Test Core` runs it.

## Acceptance notes

- **Provenance reads the sets, not the declarations.** `platform-tenant-policies.ts` keys "this is the platform's tenant policy" off the shipped sets. The ledger's copy therefore cannot go until provenance also recognises an object's declared default. Dormant today, because the copy stays. Carrier: none.
- Agents on `private` objects: a read ceiling's `'*'` does not reach `sys_verification`, `sys_jwks`, `sys_oauth_access_token` or `sys_oauth_refresh_token`, so the agent personas are refused there before any row scope applies. That is identical on both trees, and the pin lists it.
